messages.subject: Re: Predicted value nowhere near original value
parts:
On Tuesday, July 7, 2015 at 4:07:06 AM UTC-4, UD1989 wrote:


I am new in Bayesian statistics and STAN and am struggling to explain where there should be a difference in the distriution of my original dependent variable (y) and the predicted one (ynew) when same input is given.


Have you considered working with the expectations of your estimates first?  That might make it less new.  For example with the information you present below I wonder what the mean (or distribution if you want) of a[1] is.

Krzysztof
 

The use case is to predict prices of condos (y) when square-meter sizes are the independent variable (x). The heirarchial bayesian STAN model for the same is in the attachment, as well as the R code used to run it all.

in my dataset, x[1]=99 (where condo index =1) , and the corrsponding y=16000 (approx)

whereasthe following histogram is the ditribution when i do this:

ynew <- rnorm(a[1] + b * x[1] , sigma_y)
hist(ynew)




Any help will be highly appreciated ! :)
Thanks!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Predicted value nowhere near original value
parts:
> On Jul 7, 2015, at 4:07 AM, Upasana Datta <upasa...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>
>
> I am new in Bayesian statistics and STAN and am struggling to explain where there should be a difference in the distriution of my original dependent variable (y) and the predicted one (ynew) when same input is given.
>
>
>

> The use case is to predict prices of condos (y) when square-meter sizes are the independent variable (x). The heirarchial bayesian STAN model for the same is in the attachment, as well as the R code used to run it all.

How extreme do the parameters get? What's the scale of the outputs?

You are using improper priors for the hierarchical parameters, which
can cause problems.

> in my dataset, x[1]=99 (where condo index =1) , and the corrsponding y=16000 (approx)
>
> whereasthe following histogram is the ditribution when i do this:
>
> ynew <- rnorm(a[1] + b * x[1] , sigma_y)
> hist(ynew)
>

You want to draw an rnorm for each of the parameters then average.
You can do this in the generated quantities block in Stan, too.

- Bob

You're welcome.  a[1] has quite a tail which goes some way towards explaining your histogram.  You could look at the traces for all your parameters to see how that's happening.  Have you thought about whether the data you have should even be informative for the mu_a and sigma_a you are trying to estimate?

Krzysztof

Hi Bob

Thanks for your reply and help. I have added the screenshot of (some of the )outputs of parameter a[], an also some other details . I also read up on a paper talking about data similar to mine and realized that the prior distribution for a is better expressed as norm(0,sigma) and have changed my model accordingly ...this improves things raically (for example my beta values are now negative as it should be in this use case).  I will work more on this now and will post if further questions arise . BTW, could you point me to any resource which talks about evaluating the predicted values? (specifically MAPE )

Thanks again!
